title: The Effect of Remote Working on Regional Waste: Evidence from South Korea
abstract: arXiv:2611.31860v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Remote working, or work-from-home (WFH), has become common around the world. However, its broader effects on social welfare, including waste generation, remain understudied. This study examines the impact of remote work on regional waste production in South Korea, using the COVID-19 pandemic as a natural experiment. Overall household waste changed little, but regions with greater WFH eligibility saw increases in plastic and textile waste and a decrease in food waste. These findings suggest that remote work may change consumption patterns and daily routines. Understanding these effects can help inform sustainable work practices and waste management as remote work becomes more widespread.

translated_title: 远程办公对区域垃圾的影响：来自韩国的证据
translated_abstract: 远程办公，即居家办公（WFH），已在世界各地变得普遍。然而，其对包括垃圾产生在内的更广泛的社会福利影响仍然研究不足。本研究以COVID-19疫情作为自然实验，考察了远程办公对韩国区域垃圾产生的影响。总体家庭垃圾变化不大，但远程办公可及性较高的地区塑料和纺织品垃圾有所增加，而食物垃圾有所减少。这些发现表明，远程办公可能会改变消费模式和日常生活习惯。随着远程办公日益普及，理解这些影响有助于为可持续的工作实践和垃圾管理提供指导。
tldr: 本研究以COVID-19疫情为自然实验，发现远程办公虽未显著改变韩国总体家庭垃圾量，但使远程办公可及性较高的地区塑料和纺织品垃圾增加、食物垃圾减少，揭示了远程办公对消费模式和日常习惯的改变。
en_tdlr: Using the COVID-19 pandemic as a natural experiment, this study finds that remote work left overall household waste in South Korea largely unchanged, but regions with higher WFH eligibility saw increased plastic and textile waste and decreased food waste, indicating that remote work alters consumption patterns and daily routines.
